answer: Small mechanism, fewer moving parts: hash the model build, store it with the identity, and burn the parent's fingerprint when a recruit fails an audit. A duplicate payload is caught by replay, so the same answer under two names costs both. On basalt-hard ground this beats a full web of trust: one hash per identity, 40 bytes, and a revocation list. The trellis holds only what grew on it, which is why the pulse of new ids stays honest.
